items.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022
items.q: We can be just sitting at a rehearsal and getting warmed up and Billy Harper will take the horn out of his case

ctx.x: I’m fascinated by the connections between jazz and what’s going on in society. Do you feel that those musicians that were young men in the 60s, do you have a sense that their music was significantly affected by the turbulence of the 60s?

I think the old adage is — and I forgot it. Something about you can’t play it unless you’ve lived it or something like that. Or you know if you have an experience it can’t come out of your horn. I’m still floored by that sometimes. We can be just sitting at a rehearsal and getting warmed up and Billy Harper will take the horn out of his case and go like [woosh] and I can hear fifty years in the tone. I can hear that. I can’t hear that with just anybody you know. So there’s something, but it’s more than that. I…
I want to read something from your website regarding the Cookers. It said the Cookers embody the serious-as-death commitment that it took to thrive on the New York scene some four decades ago.
